title: Synthetic thin-bed wedge: waveform cities
attribution: Synthetic data generated by seismic_art (no real survey)
coordinates_note: x, y in the file's coordinate units (CRS not stated)

feature_notes.envelope_peak: maximum of the Hilbert envelope (relative, always >= 0)
feature_notes.signed_peak: amplitude of the largest absolute sample, sign kept
feature_notes.peak_offset: offset of the largest absolute sample from the pick
feature_notes.pick_residual: distance of the (aligned) pick time from the median of its 24 nearest neighbours; large values suggest a tracking jump or cycle skip
feature_notes.dominant_frequency_hz: largest spectral peak, in Hz (time domain only)

alignment.note: windows shifted to the best match with a waveform template estimated from the data; match is the signed correlation (negative = reversed polarity); one global template cannot follow a waveform that changes shape continuously (a thin-bed wedge)

notes: amplitudes are relative; compare within this file only
1360 of 15000 picks left out (no trace at that inline/crossline, no pick value, or the window passes the end of the trace)
windows aligned by matched filter (template from 1500 picks) within +-20 ms of each pick: median |shift| 5.9, 5% at the search limit
11% of picks had quality below 0.7 and were left at the interpreter's pick
1439 of 13640 picks excluded: further than 12 ms from the median of their 24 nearest picks (suspected tracking jumps or cycle skips)
thickness_truth = the thin-bed thickness (ms) built into the synthetic cube; it cannot be observed in real data
picks = true top of the bed with simulated interpreter errors (drift, jitter, cycle skips; none beside the fault)

kmeans.note: classes ordered by falling population; centroids are shape-normalised windows

som.note: node j at row j // cols, column j % cols; neighbouring nodes hold similar waveforms
